newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE FACES LEGAL CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE FACES LEGAL CHALLENGE.

text.p: Australia's fledgling Super League, already struggling to make an impact with rugby league fans, found itself at the receiving end of a legal threat on Friday from a banned player.

Former test forward Mark Geyer threatened to take media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's breakaway league to the civil courts after being suspended for 10 matches for eye-gouging and a high tackle in a match last weekend.
"To be found guilty of eye-gouging in rugby league circles is the equivalent of being called a paedophile," Geyer said. "We'll seek other avenues."
The ruling against the Perth Reds captain also prompted Geyer's lawyer to launch into an extraordinary tirade against Super League disciplinary panel.
During the hearing on Thursday evening, solicitor Chris Murphy questioned the panel's competence and independence.
"I think you're incompetent, grossly incompetent," said Murphy. "It's an utter joke, a disgrace, a kangaroo court and an idiotic process."
Super League, launched and funded in Australia by Murdoch, has failed to excite supporters after a glitzy launch last month and a costly advertising campaign.
Despite Murdoch's promise to take the game to new heights, attendances at Super League matches have fallen well below pre-launch expectations.
In a break with past practice, Super League employed three former players under the guidance of a senior lawyer to hand out suspensions for foul play.
"I think having three football players to decide this matter is a total joke. This is Mr Murdoch's court," Murphy said.
Geyer was banned for seven weeks for gouging the eyes of an Adelaide Rams player and a further three weeks for a reckless high tackle in the same match.
